create.name: Dr. Christena Cleveland
create.bio:
Christena Cleveland is a social psychologist and public theologian living in Minneapolis, Minnesota, whose teaching centres on the Black Madonna, the dark-skinned image of Mary honoured at shrines in Europe and far beyond. After a first degree at Dartmouth she took a doctorate in social psychology at the University of California, Santa Barbara, and held academic posts at several institutions, most recently Duke Divinity School, where she led its Center for Reconciliation. In 2018 she walked roughly 400 miles across central France to visit eighteen Black Madonna shrines, a journey she recounts in God Is a Black Woman (HarperOne, 2022). Her second book on the Black Madonna, published in 2026, presents her as a figure of refuge and renewal.

She founded the Black Madonna Freedom School, an online community that meets weekly across a four-year arc, with an in-person retreat in St. Paul and a pilgrimage, where students explore the sacred feminine alongside questions of race, gender and religious conditioning. Her method draws together research, storytelling, ritual and gentle somatic practice, and she welcomes people of any faith or none. She also publishes illustrated e-books of essays, art and reflective practices, leads day retreats, and speaks to congregations, universities and conferences.

books.title: God Is a Black Woman
books.author: Christena Cleveland
books.description: Her 2022 account of a 400-mile walk to Black Madonna shrines in France, combining memoir with theology and social research on how images of God shape lives.

courses.title: Black Madonna Freedom School (2027 Cohort)
courses.description: A year-long online learning community, the first of four optional years, with weekly gatherings, an in-person retreat in St. Paul and a pilgrimage. Students study the Black Madonna and the sacred feminine while working through inherited religious conditioning.

courses.title: She Who Cannot Be Shamed, Tamed or Contained
courses.description: A 95-page illustrated e-book that visits ten reimagined ancient images of the Black female divine, each paired with an essay, questions and a practice.

courses.title: Christ our Black Mother Speaks
courses.description: An 84-page illustrated collection of essays, art, questions and practices that reflects on images of Christ through the lens of the dark divine feminine.

courses.title: Not Today Colonizer
courses.description: A practical e-book on noticing and letting go of the image of God as a white man in everyday thoughts, feelings and habits, with exercises for each theme.

courses.title: Official Reflection E-Workbook for The Black Madonna
courses.description: A 65-page companion to her 2026 book, with sixteen images of the Black Madonnas it discusses and reflection questions to accompany each chapter.
